shell: shared/navigation.json#/shells/mobileStudentShell (bottom nav FULLY HIDDEN on this screen — see #/shells/mobileStudentShell/hiddenOn; this is the mobile counterpart of course-player.json's Web coursePlayerShell, but a full hide, not a 72px collapse)
routeIntent: Explore or My Learning (pushed from either) — per ux/NAVIGATION_SPEC.md § 3
sourceReferences: design-review-locked/Mentora Showcase.dc.html § 22 Product Preview — MOBILE PREVIEW "Course Player · curriculum lives in a Bottom Sheet, never beside the video" frame, lines 2234-2278 (verified by direct read)
design-review-locked/Mentora Showcase.dc.html § 19 English and Arabic — "PLAYER · EN" (lines 1707-1724) / "PLAYER · AR" (lines 1725-1744) chrome-mirrors-scrubber-stays-LTR frames

conflicts.description: shared/navigation.json#/shells/coursePlayerShell's showcaseDeviationNote (already recorded for Web) warns that the showcase's own § 17 caption over-states the Course Player exception as removing the sidebar entirely. On MOBILE specifically, this over-statement is actually CORRECT rather than an over-statement: ux/MOBILE_UX.md § 1 confirms the bottom nav really is fully hidden (not collapsed) on Course Player/Quiz — the showcase's mobile frame (lines 2234-2278) shows no nav row at all, consistent with a full hide.
conflicts.resolution: No conflict on mobile — this entry exists only to explicitly disclose that the Web-side coursePlayerShell conflict note does NOT carry over to mobile unchanged; mobile's full-hide behavior is correct as shown, not an over-statement to correct. See shared/navigation.json#/shells/mobileStudentShell/hiddenOn/platformDifferenceFromWeb for the reverse-direction disclosure (mobile differs from Web, not that mobile's own showcase evidence is wrong).

layout.$description: Single-column mobile layout — the single largest structural divergence from course-player.json's Web two-column (content-left/curriculum-right) layout, per ux/MOBILE_UX.md § 6: curriculum moves from a persistent side panel into an overlay Bottom Sheet.
topBar: course title + "Lesson N of M · X% complete" (lines 2238-2239)
Ask AI Tutor entry point (auto_awesome icon, line 2240)
layout.structure: top bar -> VideoPlayer (16:9, full width) -> lesson title -> ProgressBar -> short description -> "Course content · N / M" expandable row (triggers Bottom Sheet) -> Previous/Next lesson row
layout.curriculumBottomSheet: overlay, NOT a column — triggered by the "Course content" row; see sections[5] below

content: VideoPlayer 16:9, speed-control chip ("1×", top-end corner, line 2243) overlaid on the video itself — a mobile-only placement not present in course-player.json's Web spec, which places speed control inside the control bar only
short description (line 2256) — no Overview/Resources Tabs component on mobile, unlike Web's 2-tab structure
full-width "Course content · N / M" row: list icon (leading) + label + expand_less/more chevron (trailing) — button-styled row, not a plain link (line 2257)

chevron_left icon-only Previous button (outlined) + full-width "Next lesson" PrimaryButton with trailing chevron_right (lines 2259-2261) — no separate "Mark Complete" button visible in this frame; ux/SCREEN_UX_SPECS.md § 10 is the rank-1 authority on whether Mark Complete is a distinct action or folded into Next on mobile, not independently re-derived here
drag handle + "Course content" title + close (X) icon (lines 2264-2266)

lesson rows: check_circle (complete, success.default) / play_circle (current, brand.primaryContainer highlight) / lock_open (unlocked, not yet started) / quiz icon (module quiz row) — each row: icon + title (1-line ellipsis) + duration or question-count trailing label (lines 2268-2272)

typographyHierarchy.curriculumSectionHeading: typography.caption (showcase: font:600 12px/16px, letter-spacing 0.5px — an eyebrow treatment, not label.large as Web's course-player.json uses for its h3 section headings)

artworkRules: n/a — video content, no course-thumbnail artwork on this screen (matches course-player.json's Web rule).

exitDestinations: back to whichever tab/screen pushed this one

states.error: inline error sized to video frame, icon+title+retry (mirrors Web)
states.completion: not a separate screen state — routes to Quiz or an inline completion confirmation (mirrors course-player.json's Web note)

rtlBehavior: top bar, lesson-info block, and curriculum Bottom Sheet all mirror per logical properties — VERIFIED via § 19's "PLAYER · AR" frame (lines 1725-1744): the video control bar's icon row visually mirrors (fullscreen icon moves to the RTL-logical end via margin-inline-start:auto, not a DOM reorder) while the scrubber itself stays in an explicit dir="ltr" wrapper (line 1730) regardless of the outer dir="rtl" context — the LOCKED EXCEPTION, unchanged from Web's course-player.json rtlBehavior and shared/navigation.json#/rtlMirroring/neverMirrors/videoPlayerScrubber.
themeBehavior: video control bar tokens (color.overlay.scrim, color.text.inverse) are deliberately theme-invariant, identical to course-player.json's Web rule and shared/components.json#/videoPlayer's own description — confirmed by § 19's player frames using the same literal chrome colors regardless of the surrounding EN/AR frame's light theme.
responsiveRules: single column at every mobile width; Curriculum Bottom Sheet is a partial sheet by default (several lessons visible, scrollable, drag handle to expand toward full-height) per ux/MOBILE_UX.md § 7 — not independently re-verified live, since the showcase's own frame (lines 2263-2275) shows the sheet already in its fully-open overlay state, not the partial default height
knownGaps: The showcase's own captured Bottom Sheet frame shows it fully expanded over the whole screen (position:absolute;inset:0, line 2263) rather than the partial/several-lessons-visible default height ux/MOBILE_UX.md § 7 describes — the partial-height default behavior is asserted from that rank-1 text, not independently pixel-verified from this specific showcase frame.

No Overview/Resources Tabs equivalent is visible on mobile, unlike Web's explicit 2-tab structure (course-player.json) — ux/SCREEN_UX_SPECS.md § 10 is the rank-1 authority on whether mobile drops tabs entirely (folding Resources into the Bottom Sheet or a different affordance) or simply wasn't captured in this compact frame; not resolved here.

No mobile Dark-mode Course Player frame exists in the showcase — themeBehavior above is inferred from the general locked video-player token-invariance rule plus § 19's EN/AR (both light-theme) frames, not independently mobile-Dark-verified.
